REPORT
Date April 26, 1940.
Subject Clippings of Chinese newspapers received from Japanese
Press Censorship Bureau.
Made by D.S. Pharazyn Forwarded by Supt. Mason

With reference to the local Chinese
press clippings received from the Japanese Press
Censorship Bureau, the attached file (flagged) shows
that the first batch of these clippings was addressed
to the Commissioner of Police by the Bureau on
April 27, 1939, and since then, these clippings
enclosed in envelopes have been continually received
from the Bureau by the Commissioner of Police and
extracts from them have been duly made by this Section
and filed in the Registry after initialling by D. C.
and P. A. to D. C. (Special Branch). Up to the
present no reply on this subject has been sent to
the Bureau.

No warnings have been conveyed to the
Chinese press in relation to these extracts as
practically all of them deal with Sino-Japanese war
news and the truth or otherwise of these reports
cannot easily be verified by this office.

The few political items contained
amongst these clippings practically always receive
the attention of this Section in its own translations
and action regarding them is or is not taken depending
on instructions of D. C. (Special Branch).

D. S.
D. C. (Special Branch)

日期：1940年4月26日。
主题：从日本新闻检查局收到的中文报纸剪报。
由 D.S. Pharazyn 编制，由 Mason 警司转呈

关于从日本新闻检查局收到的本地中文报纸剪报，所附档案（已做标记）显示，该局于1939年4月27日将第一批此类剪报送交警务处处长，此后，警务处处长持续收到该局用信封封装的此类剪报，本科已对这些剪报进行摘录，并经特科副主管及特科主管助理 initials（首字母签名）后，归档至登记处。截至目前，尚未就此事项向该局发出回复。

未就这些摘录内容向中文报界发出任何警告，因为实际上所有这些内容都涉及中日战争新闻，且本处难以核实这些报道的真伪。

这些剪报中包含的少量政治项目，几乎总是受到本科在其自行翻译过程中的关注，并根据特科主管的指示决定是否对其采取行动。

TRANSLATION OF AN ARTICLE ENTITLED "THE TOWNS OF TSENG CHENG
AND TUNG KWAN DURING THE CURRENT CHINESE COUNTER-OFFENSIVE
PUBLISHED BY THE TA MEI WAN PAO

Since their withdrawal from the East River area
in Kwangtung in the middle of December 1938, the Japanese
have been holding a straight line between the towns of Tsang
Cheng and Tung Kwan which, by reason of its convenient land
and water communications, constitutes an ideal outer defensive
circle for the Japanese army.

Traffic on the railway between Canton and Kowloon
and river routes between Canton and the principal towns has
been resumed by the Japanese in co-operation with Chinese
traitors for the transportation of Japanese troops. Passengers
travelling on the railways are exceedingly few and for this
reason not much profit is being derived.

Some 2,000 Japanese troops are constantly stationed
for garrison duty in the town of Sing Toong Tseng the position
of which is of strategic importance because it commands all
lines of communication between Canton and such cities and towns
as Tseng Cheng, Shek Leung, Shek Dong, and Tung Kwan.
Some 500 men of the Japanese Artillery Regiment are billeted in
the village of Tsu Tsung situated midway between Canton and
Tseng Cheng. The stationing of these men there is to check
the activities of the Chinese guerrilla units who have often
staged surprise attacks upon the Japanese military trucks
travelling along the highway.

In order to confuse the attention of the operatives
of the Chinese Secret Service and to conceal their weakness,
the Japanese have been continuously shifting new troops
between Canton, Tsang Cheng, and the Bogue Tigris Forts.

Considerable Japanese reinforcements have arrived
at Tseng Cheng, Shek Leung, and Tung Kwan in consequence of

《大美晚报》刊登题为《当前中国反攻期间的增城与东莞城镇》的文章译文

自1938年12月中旬从广东东江地区撤退以来，日军一直据守着增城和东莞两镇之间的一条直线，由于该地区水陆交通便利，构成了日军理想的外围防御圈。

日军已与汉奸合作，恢复了广州与九龙之间的铁路交通以及广州与各主要城镇之间的内河航线，用于运输日军部队。乘坐铁路旅行的乘客极少，因此获利甚微。

约2000名日军士兵常驻守战略地位重要的新塘增城（音译）镇，该镇控制着广州与增城、石龙、石碣（音译）和东莞等城市和城镇之间的所有交通线。约500名日军炮兵团士兵驻扎在位于广州和增城中途的祖宗村（音译）。将这些士兵部署在那里是为了遏制中国游击队的活动，这些游击队经常对沿公路行驶的日军军用卡车发动突袭。

为了混淆中国特工人员的视线并掩盖其弱点，日军一直在广州、增城和虎门要塞之间不断调动新兵。

由于

the general offensive launched by the Chinese Commander of the
East River areas. These Japanese reinforcements are reported
to have come from Formosa. Their morale and fighting ability
are poor and it is expected that they will be put out of
action before long by the Chinese columns at present converging
on the town of Tseng Cheng from three sides.

It is a well known habit of the Japanese to utilize
local bad elements to form autonomous or Maintenance commissions
after occupying a district, and the same method was followed
at Tseng Cheng and Tung Kwan, where ridiculous posters, such
as "Down with the Chiang Kai-shek Regime", "Good Citizens
will be Spared", etc. have been posted every where. An
autonomous commission was established by drug merchants at
Shek Loong after the invaders had entered that town. A
number of branch commissions were formed in the neighbouring
towns. As soon as these commissions were established, the
inhabitants were required to apply for "Good Citizens
Certificates" which were issued on payment of a fee ranging
from $1.00 to few cents. In addition to the payment of this
fee, the inhabitants were also forced to defray the expenses
incurred by the various puppet organizations. The inhabitants
of Tseng Cheng are being compelled to pay $2.00 a month each
towards the upkeep of the local autonomous organizations.

Shortage of food stuffs is being experienced at
Tseng Cheng where the Japanese have seized all the food they
could lay their hands on. Japanese military notes are being
circulated in considerable amounts in the occupied areas.
The inhabitants at Shek Loong are forced to accept these notes
at the rate of $1.00 military note for $1.40 to $1.70 local
currency.

Numerous opium dens and gambling houses have
been established throughout Shek Loong, Tseng Cheng, Tung Kwan

中国东江地区指挥官发动的全面攻势，大量日军增援部队已抵达增城、石龙和东莞。据报道，这些日军增援部队来自台湾。他们的士气和战斗力低下，预计不久将被目前从三面向增城集结的中国部队消灭。

日军在占领一个地区后利用当地不良分子组建自治或维持委员会是众所周知的惯技，在增城和东莞也采取了同样的方法，到处张贴诸如“打倒蒋介石政权”、“良民不受伤害”等荒谬的海报。入侵者进入石龙（音译）镇后，由鸦片商人建立了自治委员会。邻近城镇也成立了一些分支委员会。这些委员会一经成立，居民就被要求申请“良民证”，需支付1.00美元至几角不等的费用才能签发。除了支付这笔费用外，居民还被迫承担各种傀儡组织产生的费用。增城居民正被强迫每人每月支付2.00美元，以维持当地自治组织的运作。

增城正经历食品短缺，日军搜刮了所有能到手的食物。占领区内正在大量流通日军军票。石龙居民被迫接受这些军票，汇率为1.00美元军票兑换1.40至1.70美元当地货币。

在整个石龙、增城、东莞

and Tai Ping. With a view to poisoning the minds of the
children, the Japanese have established a primary school at
Shek Loong where the Chinese children are given lessons in a
Japanese or Chinese text compiled by them.

The atrocities committed by the Japanese in areas
along the East River have left an indelible impression on the
people in these regions and will not be easily forgotten.
The Japanese are themselves fully aware of this and are doing
everything in their power to strengthen their control over
the areas they have invaded. They are spreading many rumours
with the object of undermining the unity of the people. At
the instance of the Japanese, the puppet officials have
despatched representatives to villages in the district to
induce the village elders to attend meetings convened to
consolidate control over the rural areas. While many of the
Village
elders have complied with the request of the puppets
to proceed to the towns, many have defied the puppets and
bought additional arms and ammunition to strengthen the defence
of their respective villages and to put up a stiff resistance
in the event of an attack by the Japanese military. They
would rather sacrifice their all than become slaves.

The active Chinese guerrilla units operating
mysteriously in the vicinity of Tseng Cheng and Shek Loong
have often struck terror into the hearts of the Japanese
military authorities. The Japanese have been resorting to
massacres of intellectual youths in the hope of wiping out
potential guerrillas but even in this they have had little
success. The only result achieved through other means was
an increase in the slaughter of innocent people who were put to
a cruel death on suspicion of being Chinese spies and secret
agents. The Japanese have not succeeded in finding a way to
put down the guerrillas for the latter have become more active

日军在东江沿线地区犯下的暴行给这些地区的人民留下了不可磨灭的印象，不会被轻易遗忘。日军自己也充分意识到这一点，并正在尽其所能加强对入侵地区的控制。他们散布许多谣言，旨在破坏人民的团结。在日军的指使下，傀儡官员派遣代表前往该地区的村庄，诱劝村长参加旨在巩固对农村地区控制的会议。虽然许多村长顺从了傀儡的要求前往城镇，但许多人违抗了傀儡，购买了额外的武器和弹药，以加强各自村庄的防御，并在日军进攻时进行顽强抵抗。他们宁愿牺牲一切也不愿成为奴隶。

在增城和石龙附近神秘活动的中国活跃游击队经常让日军当局感到恐惧。日军希望通过屠杀知识青年来消灭潜在的游击队员，但即使在这方面也收效甚微。通过其他手段取得的唯一结果是增加了无辜者的杀戮，这些人因涉嫌是中国间谍和特工而被残酷处死。日军未能找到镇压游击队的方法，因为后者随着时间的推移变得更加活跃

EDITORIAL COMMENT PUBLISHED BY THE ■■■ PAO:
“MILITARY VICTORY IN NORTH KIANGSE”

During the past ten days the Chinese Army has
gained unprecedented victories in North Kiangse. Kao An
and Ta Cheng have been recovered and Nanchang, Feng Sing and
Suning are being besieged. By these successes, the Japanese
plan to launch a westward drive to attack Changsha and Chuchow,
has been crushed. Their dream of isolating the Chinese 3rd
and 9th War Zones has been shattered by the Chinese victories.
The Chinese faith in the war of resistance has been strengthened
and all ideas of surrender have been blown away. These Chinese
victories are not a prelude to the forthcoming general collapse
of the Japanese invasion of China; they are an overture to
the final Chinese victory.

After their occupation of Nanchang, the Japanese
concentrated a considerable number of troops in North Kiangse
in preparation for a drive westward with Chuchow and Changsha
as their immediate objectives. The terrain of north Kiangse,
however, is not suitable for defence and the Japanese
endangered their own positions by penetrating too deeply into
the province, where they soon found themselves surrounded
from all sides by active Chinese units. This has amply shown
that the Japanese plans for an attack against Hunan are doomed
to failure.

Originally the Japanese, after occupying Nanching,
had expected to isolate the Chinese 3rd War Area and the 9th
War Area to facilitate the annihilation of the Chinese forces
at present operating in the 3rd War Area p The Chinese
menace to the various localities along the Nanking-Shanghai
and Shanghai-Hangchow Railways would also be reduced. In
addition, the traffic on the Kiangse-Chekiang Railway line
would be interrupted, and since this line connects the South-

■■■报发表的社论评论：
“赣北军事胜利”

在过去十天里，中国军队在赣北取得了前所未有的胜利。高安和大城（音译）已被收复，南昌、奉新和遂宁正被包围。通过这些胜利，日军向西推进攻击长沙和株洲的计划已被粉碎。他们孤立中国第三和第九战区的梦想因中国的胜利而破灭。中国人民对抗战的信心得到加强，所有投降的念头都已烟消云散。这些中国的胜利并非日军侵华即将全面崩溃的前奏；而是中国最终胜利的序曲。

日军占领南昌后，在赣北集中了大量部队，准备以株洲和长沙为直接目标向西推进。然而，赣北的地形不适合防守，日军因深入该省过深而危及自身阵地，很快发现自己被活跃的中国部队从四面包围。这充分表明日军进攻湖南的计划注定失败。

起初，日军在占领南京后，曾期望孤立中国第三战区和第九战区，以便歼灭目前在第三战区作战的中国部队 p 中国对京沪铁路和沪杭铁路沿线各地的威胁也将减少。此外，浙赣铁路线的交通将被中断，由于这条线路连接中国西南省份与东南地区，

The following telegrams appeared in the Sin Wan Pao(Evening
edition.), the News Digest, the Standard, the Ta Wan Pao and
the Hwa Mei Pao :-

JAPANESE ROUTED AT NANCHANG; COUNTLESS NUMBER OF
CORPSES AND AMMUNITION LEFT BEHIND; MOPPING UP
OPERATIONS NOW IN PROGRESS

Chungking - 28th:-
The news that Nanchang has been recovered
has now been confirmed by Chinese official circles here.
Nanchang is stated to have been entered by the Chinese
after a severe engagement yesterday morning. A large
quantity of arms, ammunition and foodstuffs were left
behind by the Japanese in their hasty retreat.

Chungking - 28th:-
On the 26th, the Nanchang aerodrome was
occupied by Chinese troops who then pushed on towards
Nanchang. Plain-clothes men in the city sprang into
action and engaged the Japanese in street fighting. The
Japanese retreated towards the Neu Hong Railway Station
at about midnight. Large numbers of Chinese troops
entered the city which is still burning. The Chinese
troops in the city are endeavouring to put down the fire.

Chungking - 28th:-
According to Chinese official sources,
the Chinese units which recaptured Nanchang are at present
engaged in searching for remnants of Japanese forces and
are comforting and pacifying the Chinese inhabitants.
Large numbers of Japanese dead and quantities of arms and
ammunition were left behind by the Japanese and are piled
up like mountains. The Chinese air force is daily
bombing the railway line between Nanchang and Kiukiang.
The line of communication between the retreating Japanese
army and Kiukiang has been cut.

日军在南昌溃败；留下无数尸体和弹药；扫荡行动正在进行中

重庆 - 28日：-
中国官方人士在此证实了南昌已收复的消息。据悉，中国军队在昨天上午经过激烈战斗后进入南昌。日军在仓皇撤退时留下了大量武器、弹药和食品。

重庆 - 28日：-
26日，中国军队占领了南昌机场，随后向南昌推进。城内的便衣人员采取行动，与日军展开巷战。日军在午夜左右向牛行火车站方向撤退。大批中国军队进入仍在燃烧的城市。城内的中国军队正努力灭火。

重庆 - 28日：-
据中国官方消息来源称，收复南昌的中国部队目前正致力于搜寻日军残部，并安抚中国居民。日军留下了大量尸体以及成堆如山的武器和弹药。中国空军每日轰炸南昌与九江之间的铁路线。撤退中的日军与九江之间的交通线已被切断。

WAR NEWS

Chinese forces on the eastern bank of the Kung
River (Kiangsi) advance northward.

Chinese forces in South Kwangtung re-capture
Tanchow. Japanese aerodrome outside Nanchang (Kiangsi)
actually captured by the Chinese. The right and left wings
occupy various strategic points; Fengsing is reported to have
been recaptured.

Japan sends two divisions from Formosa to attack
Swatow.

Chinese air force bomb the Bocca Tigris Forts
(Kwangtung) and sink nine Japanese warships.

Foongcheng, 28/4/39.

The vanguards of the Chinese forces advancing
upon Nanchang entered the business area of Nanchang on the
afternoon of April 27. On reaching the eastern section of
Chung Shan Road, they engaged the Japanese in furious street
fighting which was still in progress at dusk. The Chinese

Shop-keepers and residents had deposits with the Central Bank and the Bank of Communications amounting to $800,000 but the two puppet banks issued notes equal to only about one-third of the total deposits. Those who have more than $10,000 on deposit are not allowed to draw out any money.

The people must take off their hats and show respect to the Japanese sentries whenever and wherever they may be .

同蒲铁路（山西）南段的日军已多次获得增援。他们对华军的攻击未获成功，并在晋南三角地带遭受重大损失。日军军官牛岛（Ushijima）和平山（Hirayama）等人受到斥责。他们未来可能会发动新的攻击。

临汾附近正发生小规模冲突，该地仅有两千名日军。其他部队已调往南部。浮山和安泽（音译）的日军人数正在增加。

24日上午，约五百名日军在炮火掩护下入侵麦卡湾（Mae Ka Wan，色山东南），但被占据高地的中国军队击退。约两千名部队正在浮山与中国军队作战。日军军官米川（Yonegawa）日前在安巴布（An Bab，音译）阵亡。

-3-

There are 700 or 800 Japanese cavalrymen and infantrymen
at Heilungkwan. During the past few days, some 400 Japanese
were killed. The remainder are afraid to come out of their
strongholds.

The area south of Ling Shih and north of Ling Feng
has been quiet. The Japanese want to repair the highway
but they dare not do so as the Chinese troops are watching
them. The Japanese troops at Fang See will reinforce the
Japanese fighting at Heilungkwan. On the morning of 25th,
more than 1,000 Japanese troops, in two columns, advanced
southward to attack Woo Bing. They finally captured Woo
Bing as they were in larger numbers than the Chinese.

Serious fighting is still in progress in South
Shansi. The Japanese main force was repeatedly beaten off
by the Chinese. The Japanese are panic-stricken. On the
24th, 2,000 Japanese troops, equipped with 6 or 7 field guns,
advanced in four columns from Yung Cheng and attacked Wong
Ka Tsang. After six hours of fighting, the Chinese went
up the mountain and engaged the Japanese by means of Guerrilla
tactics. On the 25th, a party of Chinese troops fought
1,000 Japanese at Wong Doong Tsung (north-west of Yung Chung)
resulting in the killing of more than one hundred Japanese
within twenty-four hours. The Japanese are receiving
reinforcements from Wan Tien, but the Chinese have made
preparations to attack them again. The majority of the
Japanese at Sing Kung and Hou Moh have been sent to reinforce
the force at Yih Kou. Chinese troops will attack them on
the way. No important change in the military situation at
Wen Shi, Woo Tsing and Chi San is reported.

Tungshan - April 26.

As the Chinese have recaptured Wen Hai, Tung Yen
and Shang Shan, etc. in South Shansi, the Japanese troops

黑龙关（音译）有七八百名日本骑兵和步兵。过去几天，约四百名日军被杀。其余人员不敢走出据点。

灵石以南、临汾以北的地区保持平静。日军希望修复公路，但因中国军队监视而不敢行动。方西（Fang See，音译）的日军将增援在黑龙关作战的部队。25日上午，一千多名日军分两路纵队向南推进，进攻武兵（Woo Bing，音译）。由于人数多于中国军队，他们最终攻占了武兵。

晋南激战仍在继续。日军主力屡遭中国军队击退。日军惊慌失措。24日，两千名配备六七门野战炮的日军从运城分四路纵队推进，进攻王家藏（Wong Ka Tsang，音译）。经过六小时战斗，中国军队上山，采用游击战术与日军交战。25日，一支中国军队在永忠西北的王东庄（Wong Doong Tsung，音译）与一千名日军交战，导致一百多名日军在二十四小时内被击毙。日军正从万田（Wan Tien，音译）接收增援，但中国军队已做好准备再次攻击他们。兴公（Sing Kung，音译）和后磨（Hou Moh，音译）的大部分日军已被派往增援一口（Yih Kou，音译）的部队。中国军队将在途中袭击他们。闻喜、武清（Woo Tsing，音译）及吉三（Chi San，音译）的军事局势据报道无重大变化。

东山 - 4月26日。

随着中国军队收复晋南的文海（Wen Hai，音译）、铜岩（Tung Yen，音译）及上山（Shang Shan，音译）等地，晋南的日军

Kobayashi Detachment has lost more than two-thirds of its
strength.

The Standard publishes the following telegrams :-
CHINESE FORCES CONTINUE THEIR ENTRY INTO NANCHANG
VICTORIOUS UNITS PRAISED BY GENERALISSIMO CHIANG

Chungking - 28th.

A telegram received from Kian states that during
the past week the Chinese gained new ground in the general
offensive against Nanchang following a personal visit to the
front lines made by a certain senior officer of the Chinese
Army. At noon of the 26th, the Nanchang Aerodrome in the suburbs
of Nanchang was occupied and soon afterwards street fighting
broke out between the Chinese vanguards and the Japanese soldiers
in the city, which lasted till midnight when the Japanese
retreated towards the Neu Hong Station after setting fire to
the city. On the morning of the 27th, the entire city was
occupied by the Chinese. The Japanese at Tsingan, Fengwin
and Ani have been surrounded and are attempting to break through
by setting fire to the cities.

Changtuh, Honan - 28th.

In connection with the battle of Nanchang, General
Chiang Kai-shek has issued the following telegram to Commander
Soong of a certain Chinese Army Corps commending him for his
bravery in routing the Japanese troops:- "For their success
in the battles of Tu Kia Fee and Woocheng, General Soong of an
army corps and Divisional Commander Deeng are highly commended;
Regimental Commander Tsang Tseng Kwang of this Division is
hereby commended; for his success for defence of Woo Cheng,
and a sum of $1,000 is issued as reward for the officers and
privates of the Regiment; Divisional Commander Fu Lih Ping
is commended for his efforts in checking the southward advance
of the enemy at the Tu Kia Fee and Mu Tse Ling fronts."

《标准报》刊登以下电报：-
中国军队继续进入南昌
委座嘉奖胜利部队

重庆 - 28日。

收到吉安来电称，在中国陆军某高级军官亲自视察前线后，过去一周中国军队在对南昌的总攻势中取得了新进展。26日中午，南昌郊区的南昌机场被占领，不久后，中国先头部队与市内日军爆发巷战，战斗持续至午夜，日军在放火烧城后向牛洪站（Neu Hong Station，音译）方向撤退。27日上午，全城被中国军队占领。清江（Tsingan，音译）、丰文（Fengwin，音译）及安义（Ani，音译）的日军已被包围，正试图通过放火烧城来突围。

河南长图（Changtuh，音译） - 28日。

就南昌战役而言，蒋介石将军向某中国军军长宋发出以下电报，表彰其击溃日军的英勇表现：“鉴于在杜家费（Tu Kia Fee，音译）及吴城战役中的成功，特高度嘉奖某军军长宋将军及邓师长；特此嘉奖该师曾广团长；鉴于其在吴城防御战中的成功，特颁发一千元作为该团官兵的奖励；傅立平师长因在杜家费及穆子岭（Mu Tse Ling，音译）前线遏制敌人南进的努力而受到嘉奖。”

page_data.en:

BLUE-SKY-WHITE-SUN FLAGS FLYING THROUGHOUT THE CITY
OF NANCHANG

Chungking - 28th.
Mopping up operations are now in progress at
Nanchang by the units under the command of General Chang Tseng
after their successful entry into Nanchang. The remnants of
the Japanese Army still hiding in the city will be rounded up
and disarmed shortly. Order has been restored in the city
and the national flags are being flown every where.

Chungking - 28th. United Press.
According to a Chinese military communique, 400
Japanese soldiers were killed yesterday when the Chinese
attacked the outskirts of Nanchang. After the Chinese
occupation of the Nanchang Aerodrome outside the city, the
Japanese retreated. During the battle, the Japanese suffered
heavy casualties and loss of military supplies.

SUNG NI CHIA RECOVERED

Kweilin, Kwangse - 28th.
Sung Ni Chia was recovered by the Chinese unit
advancing in that direction. The Chinese captured two light
machine guns and scores of rifles.

青天白日旗飘扬南昌全城

重庆 - 28日。
张增将军麾下部队成功进入南昌后，目前正在南昌进行扫荡作战。仍躲藏在城内的日军残部即将被围缴械。城市秩序已恢复，各地正悬挂国旗。

重庆 - 28日。合众社。
据中国军方公报称，昨日中国军队进攻南昌郊区时，击毙四百名日军。在中国军队占领城外的南昌机场后，日军撤退。在战斗中，日军遭受重大伤亡及军用物资损失。

收复宋尼贾（SUNG NI CHIA，音译）

广西桂林 - 28日。
向该方向推进的中国部队收复了宋尼贾。中国军队缴获两挺轻机枪及数十支步枪。

The following telegram was published by the Chinese-American
Daily News:-
WOODEN FIGURES TO REPLACE LIVING SOLDIERS
Hongkong - 28th.

According to despatches from Peiping, the Japanese
military authorities have placed orders with the Lih Tah
Furniture Shop inside the Hsun Wu Gate of Peiping for the
construction of 2,000 wooden human figures to be completed
for delivery and transportation to the front on the 17-th
instant. It is said that these wooden figures will be used
by the Japanese in trenches to deceive the Chinese army.

以下电报由《中美日报》刊登：-
以木偶代替活士兵
香港 - 28日。

据北平消息，日军当局已向北平宣武门内的利达家具店订购制作两千个人形木偶，须于本月17日完成交付并运往前线。据悉，这些木偶将被日军用于战壕中以欺骗中国军队。

JAPANESE RECEIVE HEAVY BLOW IN SOUTHERN SHANSE;
ATTACKS REPULSED; MINOR SKIRMISHES STILL IN
PROGRESS IN THE VICINITY OF LINWENG;
CHINESE TROOPS IN EASTERN SUIYUAN
LAUNCH COUNTER-ATTACK

Singzih 28th cable

Successive attacks by Japanese troops
in the southern section of the Tatung-Puchow Railway during
the last two months were repeatedly repulsed with heavy losses,
especially in the vicinity of Tsi Koh, southern Shanse. The
Japanese officers-in-charge, namely (    ) & (    )
were reprimanded and they are planning another major attack.
Minor skirmishes are still in progress on both sides of
Linweng; a large part of the Japanese troops stationed at
Linweng has been transferred south, but the force at Fu San
and An Zuh have been reinforced. At daybreak of the 24th,
a body of 300 Japanese troops launched an attack on Mee Ka
Hen (south-east of Fu San), under the cover of gun-fire, but
their advance was checked at a certain highland and repulsed.
A Japanese officer by the name of Michuenchu (    )
was killed. A total of about 400 Japanese soldiers were
killed during these encounters. The warfare north of
Linweng and south of Lingzah is at a standstill. On the
25th instant a Japanese force of about 1,000 men in 2 squads,
invaded Hoping from 2 different directions and captured the
city because of numerical superiority. The Chinese are at
present holding their positions at Nientsung.

On the 24th instant, a Japanese force of
2,200 men, consisting of cavalry and infantry, accompanied
by 6 field pieces, surrounded Wong Cha Tsaung, Kiaosi (south-
west of Maowangsan) from 4 directions. A severe shelling
was lasted about 6 hours. Well knowing that the Japanese
were preparing for a decisive battle, the Chinese retired to

日军在晋南遭受重创；
攻击被击退；林温（LINWENG，音译）附近仍有小规模冲突；
绥东中国军队
发起反击

兴县28日电

过去两个月，日军在大同至蒲州铁路南段的连续攻击屡遭击退，损失惨重，特别是在晋南赤阁（Tsi Koh，音译）附近。负责的日军军官，即（    ）及（    ）
受到斥责，他们正计划另一次大规模攻击。林温两侧仍有小规模冲突；驻守林温的大部分日军已调往南部，但浮山及安泽（An Zuh，音译）的部队已得到增援。24日黎明，三百名日军在炮火掩护下进攻麦卡亨（Mee Ka Hen，浮山东南），但其推进在某高地受阻并被击退。一名名为米川中（Michuenchu，音译）的日本军官被击毙。在这些遭遇战中，共有约四百名日军被击毙。林温以北及灵扎（Lingzah，音译）以南的战事处于停滞状态。本月25日，约一千名日军分两队从两个不同方向入侵和平（Hoping，音译），并因人数优势攻占该城。中国军队目前坚守在聂村（Nientsung，音译）的阵地。

本月24日，一支由骑兵和步兵组成、配有六门野战炮的两千二百名日军部队，从四个方向包围了毛王山西南的王查庄（Wong Cha Tsaung，Kiaosi，音译）。猛烈炮击持续了约六小时。中国军队深知日军正准备决战，遂撤退至

the peaks nearby to avoid unnecessary losses.
On the evening of the 25th instant a
fight lasting one day and night took place between Chinese
and Japanese forces, the latter being estimated in the region
of 1,000 men, near Wong Tung Tsung (north-west of Yuencheng).
Some 100 Japanese were reported to have been killed. Minor
skirmishes are also reported at Vungshi, Hotsing and Mohsan.

Wuyuan, 26th cable :-
On 24th instant Chinese mobile units
operating in Eastern Suiyuan were ordered to move to border
places linking Foongzung and Liangcheng with instructions to
check the movements of the Japanese troops. Whilst in the
vicinity of Dahhaitai the Chinese encountered a party of about
200 Japanese irregulars mostly Mongols, and a fight ensued.
A section of Chinese cavalry was despatched to cut the enemy's
communications. More than half of the enemy were either
drowned or killed. Japanese reinforcements were rushed to
the scene but the Chinese had already retired.

Tungkwang, 28th cable:-
Following the recapture of Vungshi,
Tang-Ih-tsaung and Shansan by Chinese troops heavy reinforcements
were rushed to the rescue of the Japanese and bitter fighting
followed. Approximately two-thirds of a Japanese division
under Captain Kobayashi were annihilated.

附近山顶以避免不必要的损失。
本月25日晚，中日军队在永城西北的王东庄（Wong Tung Tsung，音译）附近发生了一场持续一天一夜的战斗，日军估计约有一千人。据报道约有百名日军被击毙。闻喜、霍兴（Hotsing，音译）及磨山（Mohsan，音译）也报告有小规模冲突。

五原，26日电：-
本月24日，在绥东作战的中国机动部队奉命移防至连接丰镇（Foongzung，音译）及凉城的边境地区，以遏制日军动向。在大海台（Dahhaitai，音译）附近，中国军队遭遇了一伙约两百名的日军非正规军（主要为蒙古人），随即发生战斗。一支中国骑兵分队被派去切断敌军通讯。超过半数的敌军溺亡或被击毙。日军增援部队迅速赶至现场，但中国军队已经撤退。

东光（Tungkwang，音译），28日电：-
继中国军队收复闻喜、汤义庄（Tang-Ih-tsaung，音译）及三山（Shansan，音译）后，大量增援部队被紧急调往救援日军，随之爆发激烈战斗。小林上尉指挥下的一个日军师团约三分之二被歼灭。

PUPPET POLICE COMMISSIONER, LOO YING, UNDER SURVEILLANCE;
SUSPECTED OF CONNECTION WITH THE MUTINY OF ZUNG FOH-ZAI,
GUERRILLA LEADER IN HAIMEN.
WOO TSUNG-KOO BECOMES A MONK IN PEIPING

The Japanese authorities are making investigations
into the rebellion of Zung Foh-zai, a guerrilla leader, following
the latter's pretended surrender some time ago. The Japanese
sustained heavy losses in this mutiny. It is reported that
the surrender of Zung and his men to the Japanese was accepted
on the strength of a recommendation from Loo Ying, puppet
police commissioner, and Loo is now under strong suspicion
and is being kept under strict surveillance by members of
the Japanese Special Service Section in plain clothes.
Followers of Loo are making arrangements with the Japanese
with a view to effecting Loo's liberation.

Woo Tseng-koo, who was once strongly suspected of
being involved in the attempted assassination of Soo Sih-wen,
the former Mayor of Greater Shanghai Municipality, and who
is a close follower of Loo Ying, is reported to have been
set free by the Japanese and has entered a certain monastery
in Peiping.

伪警察局长卢英受监视；
涉嫌与海门游击队首领宗福仔（Zung Foh-zai，音译）兵变有关

吴宗库在北平出家为僧

日本当局正在调查游击队首领宗福仔（Zung Foh-zai，音译）的叛乱事件，此前他曾假意投降。日军在此次兵变中遭受重大损失。据报道，宗及其部下的投降是基于伪警察局长卢英的推荐而被日军接受的，目前卢英受到强烈怀疑，并正被便衣日本特务机关成员严密监视。卢英的追随者正与日方进行安排，以期实现卢英的获释。

吴宗库（Woo Tseng-koo，音译）曾因涉嫌参与刺杀前上海特别市市长苏锡文而受到强烈怀疑，他是卢英的亲信，据报已被日方释放，并在北平某寺院出家为僧。

WANG CHING WEI IN SHANGHAI TO CONCLUDE TRAITOROUS TREATIES

It is reliably reported that Mr. Wang Ching-wei
had secretly arrived in Shanghai on or about April 24, The
Japanese Army despatched a high official to meet Wang here.
The meeting place is kept secret, even the Japanese high
officials in Shanghai had no advance information. It is
very difficult to secure information about the conference
between Mr. Wang and the Japanese official, but according to a
telegram despatched by a certain quarter from Shanghai to
Hongkong, the results are generally as follows :-
(1) Wang requests that the Japanese should not suspend their
military operations until Hengyang, Sian and Kweiling have
been captured.
(2) The proposed Central Government of Federal States to be
headed by Mr. Wang should first obtain recognition from
either Great Britain or U.S.A. or France.
(3) This Government shall organize twelve armies to fight
Chiang and the Communists with Wang as Commander-in-Chief.
(4) The organization of the Government of Federal States will
be as follows :-
(a) The Peiping Provisional Government shall be abolished
and renamed the "Autonomous Government of North
China Federated Provinces".
(b) The Nanking "Reformed Government " will be abolished
and be renamed the "Autonomous Government of East
China Federated Provinces".
(c) After Sian and the Canton-Hankow Railway have been
occupied, autonomous Governments for North-West,
Central China and South China will be established
at Sian, Wuhan and Canton respectively.

汪精卫在上海签订卖国条约

RECAPTURE OF NANCHANG

While the Japanese Forces are preparing
for a new offensive, the Chinese troops took the initiative
and launched a counter-attack which succeeded in recapturing
Nanchang, Fengsing, and Kaoan, and surrounded Wuning. Along
the borders of Hunan, Hupeh and Kiangse, the Chinese attacked
Yochow, Puchi, Yienyang, Zoongyang, Tungzung and Yangsing.
These places and others which are being attacked by the
Chinese are bases prepared by the Japanese for their new
offensive and where the Japanese main forces are concentrated.
The Chinese counter-attacks are strategic not tactical and
have succeeded in retaking the pivotal points where the
Japanese main forces are concentrated. The military strength
between China and Japan has undergone some change while the
guerrilla movement has been improved. The Japanese strength
for the new offensive has been weakened.

Subsequent to the withdrawal of the
Chinese forces from the Wuhan Area, the Japanese were able to
take Nanchang only after a lengthy period of preparation,
although their political intrigues have proved a failure.
In view of the fact that Nanchang is an important city from
the military point of view, the Japanese attack on that city
coincided with certain political intrigues. Only after the
political plans had failed that, they commenced preparations
for a new offensive. The recapture of Nanchang indicates
the strength of China's resistance and the firm attitude of the
Chinese nation.

The objects of the Chinese counter-attacks
are to intensify the guerrilla warfare, to set back the Japanese
main forces, to retake strategic points occupied by the Japanese,
and to shatter the Japanese plans for their new offensive.

收复南昌

正当日军准备发动新的攻势时，中国军队采取主动，发起反击，成功收复南昌、奉新和高安，并包围了武宁。在湖南、湖北和江西边境沿线，中国军队进攻了岳州、蒲圻、信阳、枣阳、通城和阳新。这些地点以及其他正受中国军队攻击的地方，是日军为新攻势准备的基地，也是日军主力集结之处。中国军队的反击是战略性的而非战术性的，并成功夺回了日军主力集结的关键据点。中日之间的军事力量对比发生了一些变化，游击运动得到了改善。日军用于新攻势的力量已被削弱。

在中国军队从武汉地区撤退后，日军经过长时间准备才得以占领南昌，尽管其政治阴谋已被证明失败。鉴于南昌在军事上是一座重要城市，日军对该城的攻击与某些政治阴谋相配合。只有在政治计划失败后，他们才开始准备新的攻势。南昌的收复表明了中国抵抗的力量和中华民族的坚定态度。

中国军队反击的目标是加强游击战，阻滞日军主力，夺回被日军占领的战略要点，并粉碎日军的新攻势计划。

Hongkong, April 27.
A telegram received from Chungking this morning
states that according to a report from the front, Chinese
troops on the evening of April 25 made an assault on Nanchang
and after a night of severe fighting, recaptured the city.
Chinese troops are now "mopping up" the remnants of
Japanese soldiers.

Changsha, April 27.
On the morning of April 26, six Chinese aeroplanes
bombed Japanese positions at Fenghsin (奉新) and inflicted
heavy losses on the Japanese soldiers before flying over
Nanchang and disseminating copies of a handbill containing
an open letter addressed to Japanese soldiers.

bombers of the Chinese airforce on April 25, the Japanese
soldiers who were concentrated at Kiukiang and were ready to
reinforce the troops at Nanchang became very disorderly.

Standard publishes the following editorial:

THE VICTORY OVER NANCHANG

Nanchang has been recovered. This report of victory will be the prelude of the failure of Japan in her aggressive military operations against China.

It inspires everyone with the best of spirits to hear of the victory over Nanchang because through this victory the weak strength of the Japanese main forces has been exposed, and the failure in the war tactics of the Japanese military authorities has been proved. Furthermore, despite repeated victories and reports of the recovery of lost territories by the Chinese forces during the past some 20 months, the recapture of an important point like Nanchang is an unprecedented act.

As witness the result of this battle, the final victory will be China's and nobody should entertain any doubt of it.

We must understand that the launching of offensives by the Chinese troops at various fronts at present does not necessarily mean the commencement of a general counter-offensive against the Japanese. The principal object in the second stage of the war of resistance is to stop the attacks launched by the Japanese and to occupy the points that are to be placed under Chinese control prior to a general counter-offensive. With undaunted spirit and patience as well as concentration of the strength of the people throughout the country, China can attain her object of recovering all lost territories.

The victory over Nanchang will undoubtedly encourage the spirit of the Chinese people in fighting against the aggressors to the bitter end.

南昌大捷

南昌已收复。这一胜利报道将成为日本对华侵略军事行动失败的序幕。

听到南昌大捷的消息令每个人精神振奋，因为通过这次胜利，日军主力的薄弱实力暴露无遗，日本军方的战争战术失败也得到了证明。此外，尽管在过去约20个月里，中国军队屡获胜利并有关于收复失地的报道，但像南昌这样的重要据点的收复是前所未有的举动。

以此战结果为证，最终胜利属于中国，任何人都不应对此存有疑虑。

我们必须明白，目前中国军队在各战线发起的进攻并不一定意味着对日全面反攻的开始。抗日战争第二阶段的主要目标是阻止日军发动的攻击，并在全面反攻之前占领那些置于中国控制之下的据点。凭借无畏的精神、耐心以及全国人民力量的集中，中国能够实现收复所有失地的目标。

南昌大捷无疑将鼓舞中国人民战斗到底、抗击侵略者的精神。

Ta Mei Wan Pao publishes the following editorials

A MILITARY PACT BETWEEN GERMANY, JAPAN
AND ITALY

Much has been talked about the conclusion of a
military pact between Germany, Japan and Italy; however, none
of the governments have given any indication in this
connection. According to a United Press telegram from Tokyo
dated April 24, magnates in financial circles in Japan are
opposed to the matter, and even certain militarists have
withdrawn their support and advocated a steady policy. If
this information of the United Press is actually reliable,
the conclusion of a military pact between Germany, Japan and
Italy would probably prove futile.

It will be the same to China whether or not Japan
joins the military pact. Japan joins the pact simply
because she could do what she likes in case of war breaking
out in Europe. If she fails to join the pact, she is
prepared to fight a life-and-death battle with China.

It is apparent that China will not change her tactics
because of the non-participation of Japan in the military
pact. The object of China's war of resistance is to make
Japanese militarists come to their senses and to stop their
aggressive activities against a peaceful nation. If the war
of resistance continues, there will come a day when Japan
will be compelled to abandon her aggressive policy against China.

As Japan has no intention to join the military pact,
we can see that China has done something for world peace
through her war of resistance. It is necessary for the
various Powers in Europe to intensify their movement to
support China, economically, militarily and politically, to
enable her to accomplish her final mission.

德日意军事协定

关于德国、日本和意大利缔结军事协定的传闻甚嚣尘上；然而，各国政府均未就此发表任何声明。据合众社4月24日从东京发出的电报称，日本金融界巨头反对此事，甚至某些军国主义分子也撤回支持，主张采取稳健政策。如果合众社的这一消息确实可靠，那么德日意三国缔结军事协定恐怕将是徒劳之举。

无论日本是否加入该军事协定，对中国而言结果都是一样的。日本加入协定，仅仅是因为一旦欧洲爆发战争，它便可随心所欲地行动。如果它不加入协定，它已准备好与中国进行生死搏斗。

显然，中国不会因日本未参加军事协定而改变其策略。中国抗战的目的是使日本军国主义者清醒过来，停止对一个和平国家的侵略活动。如果抗战继续下去，终有一天日本将被迫放弃其对华侵略政策。

既然日本无意加入军事协定，我们可以看出，中国通过抗战为世界和平做出了一些贡献。欧洲列强有必要加强在经济、军事和政治上支持中国的运动，以使中国能够完成其最终使命。

UNEMPLOYED JAPANESE ATTEMPTS TO COMMIT
"HARAKIRI"

On the morning of April 26, a Japanese named Inouye
attempted to commit "harakiri" in a passage in the S.M.C.
Administration Building. He had been unemployed for some
time, and believing the propaganda of the Japanese Government
to the effect that any Japanese who went to Shanghai, a place
of gold, would become rich, he arrived here on April 15.

Unexpectedly, after arrival, he became very disappointed
as he was unable to obtain employment. He realized that it
was harder to find work in Shanghai than in Japan.

Yesterday was the date on which he had to pay his
rent for his accommodation on Boene Road. Having no money,
he left his house in order to avoid meeting his chief tenant
and went to the area south of the Soochow Creek. On seeing
the offices of the S.M.C., he entered and after inspecting
various departments, he came to the entrance of the Finance
Department where he noticed piles of banknotes which made him
feel very envious and indignant. As a result, the Japanese
sat by the side of the staircase, where he undid his clothing
and cut open his stomach with a knife.

It is learned that he was sent to the Pooming Hospital
for treatment where it was found on examination that his
injuries were not serious.

失业日本人企图“切腹”

4月26日上午，一名叫井上（Inouye）的日本人在工部局行政大楼的一条过道里企图“切腹”。他已失业一段时间，因相信日本政府宣传所谓任何前往上海这个“黄金之地”的日本人都会发财的说法，于4月15日抵达此地。

出乎意料的是，抵达后他非常失望，因为无法找到工作。他意识到在上海找工作比在日本更难。

昨天是他必须支付波恩路（Boene Road）住宿租金的日子。由于身无分文，为了避开房东，他离家出走，前往苏州河以南地区。看到工部局的办公处后，他走了进去，在视察了各个部门后，来到财务处入口，注意到成堆的钞票，这使他感到既羡慕又愤慨。于是，这名日本人坐在楼梯旁，解开衣服，用刀剖开腹部。

据悉，他被送往宝隆医院（Pooming Hospital）接受治疗，经检查发现伤势并不严重。

Shun Pao publishes the following article:

IN A REEDY GROVE - A NIGHT IN CHAO KIA DOO

Chao Kia Doo is the name of a ferry landing place
along the Whangpoo. On a certain night, a boat can be seen
in the vicinity of the landing place, being rowed on the
river towards the shore under a pale moon. Several men
clad in yellow clothes are dimly visible on board the boat;
they are all armed with rifles with eyes wide open like those
of vultures staring into the surrounding darkness. Some-
times they whistle in a happy mood while sometimes they
burst into laughter.

In a reedy bed near the shore, footsteps can be
heard wading in the water.

----- "Come on! Get ready! The boat of the
devils is coming nearer!"

An order is given, which is followed by a moment's
whisper in the reedy bed, then everything is quiet again.

The little boat is getting nearer to the shore.
Another burst of happy laughter emanates from the group on
board the boat.

"Bang!"

Following this first shot, a hail of bullets rings
through the reedy grove in the darkness. They find their
way to their target - the boat.

When the men in yellow clothes have recovered from
the shock, placed their rifles in position and taken aim,
they find that two of their number have already fallen flat.
A pool of red blood flows from the boat into the river.

Volley after volley of bullets fly between the
bed of reeds and the boat aimlessly.

芦苇丛中——赵家渡之夜

赵家渡是黄浦江沿岸一个轮渡码头的名称。在某天夜晚，可以看到一艘小船在码头附近，在苍白的月光下划向岸边。船上隐约可见几名身穿黄衣的人；他们都持有步枪，双眼圆睁，如同秃鹫般凝视着周围的黑暗。他们有时愉快地吹着口哨，有时则放声大笑。

在靠近岸边的芦苇荡中，可以听到涉水而行的脚步声。

----- “来吧！准备好！鬼子的船靠近了！”

一声令下，芦苇荡中传来一阵低语，随后一切重归寂静。

小船正驶近岸边。船上的人群再次爆发出一阵欢快的笑声。

“砰！”

随着第一声枪响，密集的子弹在黑暗中穿过芦苇丛呼啸而过。它们找到了目标——那艘船。

当黄衣人从震惊中恢复过来，架起步枪并瞄准时，他们发现其中两人已经倒地不起。一滩鲜血从船上流入河中。

一排排子弹漫无目的地在芦苇荡和小船之间飞来飞去。

An hour later, the mad exchange of shots is over and
the air becomes calm again. A capsized boat is found floating
on the Whangpoo; several corpses float in the midst of the
froth and waves of the river. Red blood mingles with the
muddy river water.

Red blood also flows into the river from the reedy
bed. Several men are heard groaning in agony, but their
groaning can hardly be heard as the others in the grove shout
in joy and sing songs in triumph.

Now comes the dawn. The morning sun shines into the
reedy bed.

一小时后，疯狂的交火结束，空气再次平静下来。人们发现一艘翻覆的小船漂浮在黄浦江上；几具尸体漂浮在江面的泡沫和波浪之中。鲜红的血液与浑浊的江水混合在一起。

鲜血也从芦苇荡中流入江中。听到几个人在痛苦中呻吟，但由于芦苇丛中其他人欢呼雀跃、高唱胜利之歌，他们的呻吟声几乎听不见。

此刻黎明来临。晨光照进芦苇荡。

Shun Pao publishes the following comment:

THE HIGHLY STIMULATING FACT

During the past few days a great deal of excitement
has been stirred up by the fact that the City of Nanchang has
been recovered and that British Conscription has been announced.
We rejoice over the victory at Nanchang not because of
the fact that a city which had fallen to the enemy has now
been recovered, but rather because this victory indicates amply
that the Chinese strength is still quite capable of winning
battles and recovering cities.
As to the British Conscription, we are happy to note
that Mr. Chamberlain is now determined to lead the British
Empire in Checking the ambitions of the aggressive nations.
In view of the foregoing facts, we earnestly hope that
the people of China will observe their task more clearly and
redouble their efforts so as to ensure the final victory.
We also hope that the British authorities should have learned
a valuable lesson from the humiliating experience that Sir Neville
Henderson, the British Ambassador to Berlin was made to undergo
when his request to interview Herr Hitler and the Reich Foreign
Minister upon his return to Berlin were refused by the latter.
We believe that spiritual strength surpasses everything
else. The determination to carry on our present task will
eventually bring about an early victory.

日本外交何去何从？

不可否认，日本是一个充满矛盾的国家。日本在意识形态上是一个民主国家，但实际上却是军事独裁。从经济上讲，日本实行资本主义制度，但日本资本家和金融家并不受军国主义者，尤其是目前控制日本政治的年轻军官们的青睐，这些年轻军官的理论类似于社会主义学说。在外交领域，日本是《反共产国际协定》的签署国之一，因此本应站在德国和意大利组成的统一战线一边，但它又不愿放弃与民主阵线国家——英国、法国和美利坚合众国的友谊。

日本正面临两难境地。尽管日本政府最高当局召开并举行了多次会议，但就是否应与德国和意大利结成军事同盟，还是与民主国家达成和解，尚未做出任何决定。显然，日本政府内部存在分歧。两种不同意见的代表分别是：那些凭借谨慎和经验主张日本在当前情况下应避免与德国和意大利结成军事同盟的老政治家，以及那些执意继续其挑战民主国家、威胁其在远东权利和利益的错误行径的年轻军官。

December 4. The strength of the
Japanese troops in Fengsin (奉新) and
Tsingan (靖安) in Kiangsi is 3000.
The Japanese military authorities will
launch a further attack as soon as
reinforcements arrive.

4. The National Herald
CHINESE BESIEGE JAPANESE IN NANNING

Following the capture of Nanning
(南寧), the Japanese authorities, in
an endeavour to strengthen their defence
immediately arranged to advance towards
Wuming (武鳴) and Pingyang (賓陽).
However, this was frustrated by the
counter-attack of the Chinese. The
latter successfully recaptured several
strategic points along the highway near
Nanning and Wutang (五塘) and surround-
ed the Japanese in Nanning. Furious
page_data.zh:
-3-

金田 (金田)，安徽省伪政府警察局警务处处长，也是唐肖侯的亲信。金曾任津浦线蚌埠段的铁路警卫队长。

3. 《华美晚报》
日军在奉新遭遇强烈抵抗

据中方消息来源称，12月3日，驻奉新的日军对江西白马廊和富贵桥的中国军队据点发动了猛烈攻击。中国士兵进行了顽强抵抗，并于12月4日晚击退了敌人。江西奉新和靖安的日军兵力为3000人。一旦援军到达，日本军方将发动进一步攻击。

4. 《申报》
中国军队包围南宁日军

继占领南宁后，日本当局为加强防御，立即安排向武鸣和宾阳推进。然而，这一企图因中国军队的反攻而受挫。后者成功收复了南宁和五塘附近公路上的几个战略要点，并包围了南宁的日军。激烈的

page_data.en:
-4-

fighting is in progress.

5. The National Herald MYSTERIOUS DEATH OF GENERAL WU PEI-FU
(Chungking telegram - Associated Press):-
The message of the death of
General Wu Pei-fu has brought great
mourning among official circles. The
Government officials are attempting to
find a key to this mysterious death as
the late General Wu was reported to have
been suffocated during the operation of
tooth extraction by a Japanese doctor
whose countrymen attempted in vain to
persuade General Wu to be a puppet leader.

6. China Evening News CHINESE RECAPTURE WUTANG AND CHANGAN
(Chungking telegram):-
It is reported that the Chinese
forces in south Kweichow have launched a
fierce counter attack on the Japanese
invaders and successfully recaptured
Wutang and Changan today. The Japanese
sustained a heavy loss in both lives and
ammunitions. Japanese soldiers in Nanning
were surrounded by Chinese troops.

7. Ta Mei Pao DEATH OF GENERAL WU PEI-FU
(Hongkong telegram of December 5):-
According to information from
Peiping and Tientsin, the late General
Wu Pei-fu fell ill due to Japanese
oppression, as he was greatly annoyed
by visits of the Japanese special
servicemen. At about 4.45 p.m. on
December 4, 1939, Japanese doctors

-4-

战斗正在进行中。

5. 《申报》 吴佩孚将军神秘死亡
（重庆电 - 美联社）：-
吴佩孚将军的死讯在官方圈子中引起了巨大的悲痛。政府官员正试图揭开这一神秘死亡的真相，因为据报道，已故吴将军是在一名日本医生进行拔牙手术时窒息身亡的，而该医生的同胞曾试图说服吴将军担任傀儡领袖，但未成功。

6. 《字林西报》晚刊 中国军队收复五塘和长安
（重庆电）：-
据报道，驻贵州南部的中国军队对日本侵略者发动了猛烈反攻，并于今日成功收复五塘和长安。日军在人员和弹药方面遭受重创。南宁的日军被中国军队包围。

7. 《大美报》 吴佩孚将军之死
（香港12月5日电）：-
据来自北平和天津的消息，已故吴佩孚将军因受日本压迫而生病，他对日本特务人员的频繁拜访感到极为恼火。1939年12月4日下午4点45分左右，日本医生

page_data.en:
-5-
were seen entering and leaving General
Wu's residence which was under heavy
guard by Japanese Gendarmes. According
to a German surgeon of Peiping, the
late General Wu's death was the fault
of the Japanese dentists.

被看到进出吴将军的住所，该住所由日本宪兵严密把守。据北平的一位德国外科医生称，已故吴将军的死是日本牙医的过错。

1. Hwa Pao.
CHINESE ARMY IN SIHHSIEN CONTINUES FURTHER
ADVANCE
(Loyang telegram of 28/12/39):-
According to a report from Chinese sources,
three main points such as Licheng, Tungyangkwan
and Sihhsien have been captured by the Chinese
army. The Japanese are uneasy since their
communication lines in Honan and Shansi
provinces have been completely cut by the
Chinese.
(Shanchow telegram of 29/12/39):-
According to a statement received from Chinese
sources, after three days of serious fighting
the Chinese army completely captured west Likao
and other main points nearby Changtze. All
counter-attacks made by the Japanese army
ended in failure. About 1,500 Japanese
soldiers were killed in this engagement. At
the moment serious fighting is still going on.
(Hsingtsi telegram of 28/12/39):-
A Chinese report states that on 26/12/39
the Chinese army occupied Yuhsiang, Tungching
and Hwacheng and destroyed many Japanese camps
and puppet organizations. When the Japanese
reinforcement arrived from Lingchin, the
Chinese army safely withdrew. The Japanese army
south of Haishsien and Hsienkuko district was
bitterly attacked by the Chinese and sustained
heavy casualties.
The number of puppet soldiers who surren-
dered to the Chinese army has considerably
increased. On 14/12/39 25,000 puppet soldiers
stationed in five districts in north Hopei
rebelled, according to a Chinese political
statement here.
page_data.zh:
1. 《华报》。
泗县中国军队继续推进
（洛阳1939年12月28日电）：-
据中方消息来源报道，黎城、东阳关和泗县等三个主要据点已被中国军队占领。由于其在河南和山西的通讯线路被中国军队完全切断，日军感到不安。
（山州1939年12月29日电）：-
据从中方收到的声明称，经过三天的激烈战斗，中国军队完全占领了长子附近的西李高及其他主要据点。日军发动的所有反攻均以失败告终。此次交战中共有约1,500名日军士兵被击毙。目前激战仍在继续。
（兴集1939年12月28日电）：-
一份中方报告称，1939年12月26日，中国军队占领了榆社、桐城和化城，并摧毁了许多日军营地和伪组织。当日军增援部队从陵川到达时，中国军队安全撤离。海县和仙居口地区以南的日军遭到中国军队的猛烈攻击，伤亡惨重。
向中國軍隊投降的偽軍士兵數量顯著增加。據此間的一份中國政治聲明稱，1939年12月14日，駐紮在冀北五個地區的25,000名偽軍士兵發動了叛變。

-2-

2. The National Herald. JAPANESE ARMY SUFFERS HEAVY CASUALTIES IN
NANCHANG
(Tunghsiang telegram of 29/12/39):-
As a result of attacks repeatedly made by
the Chinese army, the Japanese army in Nanchang
suffered more than 2,000 casualties. About
1,000 Japanese wounded soldiers have been
removed from Lientang to Nanchang.

3. Shun Pao. (Tunghsiang):-
According to a reliable report, about
3,500 Japanese wounded soldiers have been
removed from the suburbs to Nanchang.

4. Shun Pao. JAPANESE SUFFER HEAVY LOSSES IN KWOONLUNGKWAN
FIGHTING
(Liuchow telegram of 29/12/39):-
The Japanese army in Kwoonlungkwan
suffered extremely heavy casualties.
Kwoonlungkwan was retaken by the Chinese.
A Japanese soldier's note-book was found, in
which their defeats, the names of their
officers killed in battle and also their
admiration for the fighting spirit of the
Chinese soldiers were recorded.

5. Chinese-American JAPANESE ATTACK ON PEIHIANG FAILS:
Daily News. MORE THAN 2,000 CASUALTIES SUSTAINED.
(Voongyuan and Kweilin telegram of 28/12/39):-
The Chinese attacked the Japanese at
Neupeichi. In the course of this engagement
several hundred Japanese soldiers were killed
and many men captured. On 27/12/39 Japanese
reinforcements arrived but were defeated. The
Japanese lost 200 motor cars and sustained more
than 2,000 casualties.
page_data.zh:
-2-

2. 《申报》。 日军在南昌遭受重大伤亡
（东乡1939年12月29日电）：-
由于中国军队的反复攻击，南昌日军伤亡超过2,000人。约1,000名日本伤兵已从莲塘转移至南昌。

3. 《申报》。（东乡）：-
据可靠消息，约3,500名日本伤兵已从郊区转移至南昌。

4. 《申报》。 日军在昆仑关战斗中遭受重大损失
（柳州1939年12月29日电）：-
昆仑关的日军遭受了极其惨重的伤亡。昆仑关已被中国军队收复。发现了一本日军士兵的笔记本，其中记录了他们的失败、阵亡军官的姓名以及他们对中国士兵战斗精神的钦佩。

5. 《中美日报》 日军进攻北乡失败：
伤亡超过2,000人。
（融元和桂林1939年12月28日电）：-
中国军队在新北池攻击日军。在此次交战中，数百名日军士兵被击毙，多人被俘。1939年12月27日，日军增援部队到达，但被击败。日军损失了200辆汽车，伤亡超过2,000人。

-3-

The Japanese army retreating from Meikong
to Chinchuyuan was encircled and attacked by
the Chinese and sustained heavy casualties.
At the moment serious fighting is still taking
place.
(Telegram of 28/12/39 from a certain place
of North Canton):-

After heavy attacks made by the Chinese,
the Japanese army advancing towards Chingyuan-
hsien (Tienhsin district) was forced to retreat
to Kaotien, about 10 li west of Tienhsin.
(Yingteh telegram of 28/12/39):-

The Japanese army retreating to the south
coast of Peikiang was bitterly attacked by the
Chinese and lost many lives. On 27/12/39
the Japanese army retreated to Hwahsien and
was attacked by the Chinese.
(Chaoking telegram of 28/12/39):-

On 24/12/39 the Chinese army attacked
Kiangmen and Mayuan. The Japanese were defeated
On 25/12/39 the Chinese advanced through
Mayuan and dashed into Kiangmen city where they
opened street fighting which lasted two hours.
The Japanese suffered heavy losses. However,
when Japanese reinforcements arrived, the
Chinese had safely retired. Many camps, sta-
bles and various structures were burned down
by the Chinese.
(Hongkong Intelligence News Agency telegram
of 28/12/39):-

According to information received from
Canton, a Japanese spokesman has publicly
confirmed the report that the attempts of the

从梅坑（Meikong）撤退至金竹园（Chinchuyuan）的日军遭到中国军队包围和攻击，伤亡惨重。目前激战仍在进行。
（1939年12月28日发自粤北某地的电报）：-

在中国军队的猛烈攻击下，向清远县（田心区）推进的日军被迫撤退至田心以西约10里的高田（Kaotien）。
（1939年12月28日英德电报）：-

向南撤至北江沿岸的日军遭到中国军队的猛烈攻击，死伤众多。1939年12月27日，日军撤退至花县并遭到中国军队攻击。
（1939年12月28日肇庆电报）：-

1939年12月24日，中国军队攻击江门和马园。日军战败。1939年12月25日，中国军队经马园推进，冲入江门市内，展开持续两小时的巷战。日军遭受重大损失。然而，当日军增援部队到达时，中国军队已安全撤离。许多营房、马厩和各种建筑物被中国军队焚毁。
（1939年12月28日香港情报新闻社电报）：-

据从广州收到的消息，一位日本发言人公开证实了如下报道：

Japanese army to penetrate into Peikiang have
proved a failure. The Japanese have given up
many points in the area north of Canton. No
improvement can be made by the Japanese to their
position, as the main force of the Chinese army
are gathered to the north of Canton.
(Chungking Associated Press telegram of 28/12/39):-
According to a Chinese political spokesman
today, serious fighting took place at Takaofeng
in the area between Nanning and Wuming. He
denied that the Japanese army had approached
Chengnankwan near Lungchow because the Japanese
army was defeated by the Chinese before they
could reach their destination.
Lately two Divisions of the Japanese army
made attempts to penetrate into the area north
of Canton but were held up by the Chinese army

6. Hwa Pao. NATURAL CALAMITY AND ANTI-WAR MOVEMENT IN JAPAN.
(Hongkong telegram of 27/12/39):-
According to a certain foreigner arriving
from Japan, there is a shortage of rice and other
food stuffs in Japan owing to the recent
calamities of nature that have occurred in Japan.
Instructions were issued by the Japanese
Government forbidding her people to hoard food.
The anti-war movement has also become very
active in Kobe. On 13/12/39 quantities of military
supplies were burned by rioters while a munition
depot in Formosa was destroyed on 11/12/39.

日军渗透进入北江的企图已被证明失败。日军已放弃广州以北地区的许多据点。由于中国军队主力集结于广州以北，日军无法改善其处境。
（1939年12月28日重庆合众社电报）：-

据一位中国政治发言人今日称，在南宁与武鸣之间的地区，大高峰（Takaofeng）发生了激战。他否认日军已接近龙州附近的镇南关，因为日军在到达目的地之前就被中国军队击败。
最近，日军两个师团试图渗透进入广州以北地区，但在清华（Tsinghua）、龙门和良口（Liangkow）被中国军队阻挡。
6. 《华报》。日本的自然灾害与反战运动。
（1939年12月27日香港电报）：-
据一位从日本抵达的外国人称，由于日本近期发生的自然灾害，日本国内大米和其他食品短缺。日本政府已发布指令，禁止民众囤积粮食。神户的反战运动也变得非常活跃。1939年12月13日，暴徒烧毁了大量军用物资；1939年12月11日，台湾的一个弹药库被摧毁。

7. The National Herald. CHINESE ARMY IN SOUTH SECTION OF CANTON-HANKOW
RAILWAY WINS BIG VICTORY
(Hongkong Special telegram of 28/12/39);-
(Kweilin). The Japanese cavalry at Yung-Lung
Highway was completely annihilated by the
Chinese army yesterday. The remnant of about
1,000 Japanese soldiers of the Japanese 3rd
Division were badly beaten by the Chinese army
at Shanyueh in the vicinity of Suilu. There
are no Japanese soldiers in the vicinity of
Lungchow.

8. Chinese-American CHINESE ARMY AT SOUTH END OF CANTON-HANKOW
Daily News: RAILWAY WINS BIG VICTORY
(Hongkong special telegram of 3/1/40):-
Fighting has been intensified in North
Canton. General Chiang Kai-shek has issued a
telegraphic message to General Yu Han Mo direct-
ing military operations. While sending $20,000
to reward the Chinese army, the Central Govern-
ment has also despatched reinforcements to
North Canton.
(Telegram of 2/1/40 from a certain point on
North Canton front):-
(1). One brigade of the Japanese Central Route
army was completely swept away by the Chinese
army and the two wings of the Japanese army
retreated.
(2). The Japanese army in Tsengcheng sustained
heavy casualties as a result of attacks recently
made by the Chinese army. The Chinese army
captured Meikong, Neupeichi and other important
points in the vicinity.
(3). The remainder of the Japanese army near the
Canton-Hankow Railway retreated southward on

7. 《国民日报》。粤汉铁路南段中国军队取得大胜
（1939年12月28日香港特约电报）：-
（桂林）。昨日，永龙公路上的日军骑兵被中国军队全歼。日军第三师团约1000名残兵在遂流（Suilu）附近的山岳（Shanyueh）被中国军队重创。龙州附近已无日军士兵。

8. 《中美日报》：粤汉铁路南端中国军队取得大胜
（1940年1月3日香港特约电报）：-
粤北战事加剧。蒋介石将军已向指挥军事行动的余汉谋将军发出电报指示。中央政府除拨款2万美元奖励中国军队外，还向粤北派遣了增援部队。
（1940年1月2日发自粤北前线某地的电报）：-
(1). 日军中路军的一个旅被中国军队彻底消灭，日军两翼撤退。
(2). 由于中国军队最近的攻击，增城（Tsengcheng）的日军伤亡惨重。中国军队占领了梅坑（Meikong）、牛鼻池（Neupeichi）及附近其他重要据点。
(3). 粤汉铁路附近的日军残部于

the morning of 2/1/40 and suffered very heavy
casualties. Many rifles were seized by the Chinese
army.
(4). The Japanese army in Kwantu was encircled
and attacked by the Chinese army on 1/1/40 and
sustained heavy casualties. When the remainder
of the Japanese army retreated southward, they
were followed by the Chinese.
(5). According to a local statement, the Japanese
army engaged in attacking Voongyuan comprised
several thousands each of infantry and cavalry.
(Chackwan telegram of 2/1/40):-
The Japanese army attacking Voongyuan was
defeated by the Chinese and retreated southward.
The vanguard of the Japanese army in the vicinity
of Liangkowyu was completely destroyed.
(Chungking telegram of 3/1/40):-
Three divisions, one united brigade and a
naval landing party of the Japanese army comprising
more than 10,000 soldiers gathered at Tsaoshan and
Shunchuan for the destination of Chackwan. However,
they were encircled and attacked by the Chinese army
and retreated southward, leaving more than 3,000
casualties in the vicinity of Kingchuyuan and Satien,
more than 2,000 in the area of Neupeichi and Lutien,
about 1,000 in the vicinity of Lienkiangkow and
Pakiangkow and many other points. Many Chinese
innocent people were ruthlessly killed by the
Japanese army when they were retreating from place
to place and also many houses were burned down by
them. The Japanese suffered total losses of more
than 10,000 casualties.

1940年1月2日上午向南撤退，伤亡极为惨重。中国军队缴获了许多步枪。

日军三个师团、一个联合旅团以及一支海军陆战队，共计一万多名士兵，集结于草山（Tsaoshan）和顺川（Shunchuan），意图前往赤坎。然而，他们被中国军队包围并攻击，向南撤退，在井竹园（Kingchuyuan）和沙田（Satien）附近留下3000多名伤亡人员，在牛鼻池（Neupeichi）和鹿田（Lutien）地区有2000多名，在连江口（Lienkiangkow）和白江口（Pakiangkow）附近及其他许多地点约有1000名。日军在四处撤退期间残忍杀害了许多中国无辜平民，并烧毁了许多房屋。日军总伤亡人数超过10,000人。
